content.title: About
content.content: A turkey sandwich or sub is a sandwich that uses roasted or smoked turkey as the main filling, often combined with lettuce, tomato, cheese, avocado, and various sauces. It is served on a long roll or baguette and is popular in fast‑food restaurants and cafés.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is considered a leaner meat compared with chicken and beef.
Sub sandwiches got their name from “submarine” because the rolls resemble a submarine’s shape.
In the United States, turkey subs are frequently served with cranberry sauce or mustard.
Turkey was domesticated in Mexico over 2,000 years ago and is now exported worldwide.
Some eateries add bacon strips to the sandwich for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Turkey provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other meats, turkey has a low amount of saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey contains vitamins B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Turkey supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Selenium in turkey contributes to antioxidant protection and immune system strength.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked turkey may harbor salmonella; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sandwiches often contain salty sauces and processed meat, raising sodium levels.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to bird meat, which can cause skin reactions or breathing difficulties.

items.title: High calories with add‑ons
items.content: Cheese, sauces, and bacon can significantly increase calories and fat content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey sandwiches are usually cut in half and eaten by hand. They can be topped with fresh vegetables, avocado, mustard, mayo, or hummus. For a lighter option, choose a whole‑grain roll and a low‑fat sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A prepared sandwich can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Keep the turkey and sliced veggies separate from the roll to prevent sogginess.
